The design is now fixed and all tests pass.

I found two bugs in `rtl/hamming_secded.v`:
1. `syn` in 13–15 with `parity=1` (uncorrectable multi-bit error, spec rule 4) was being misclassified as a correctable single error instead of `double_err`.
2. The data-bit `flip` correction was applied based on `syn` alone, so in double-error cases (`parity=0`) where `syn` happened to match a data-bit position, `data` was incorrectly "corrected" instead of being passed through unmodified (spec rule 5).

Both are fixed by gating correction/flip on `correctable = parity && (syn <= 12)`. The visible testbench (`tb_visible.v`) passes with `TEST PASSED`, and I additionally verified exhaustively over all 8192 possible 13-bit codewords that the uncorrectable (`syn` 13–15) and double-error (`parity=0`, `syn≠0`) cases now behave per spec, with no discrepancies found.
